title: Our favorite space and sci-fi Playmobil sets: From Star Trek playsets to ESA-collaborated models
summary: Here are 13 of Playmobil's space and sci-fi sets — you'll be sure to find something to suit your needs.
contentText:
Playmobil is known for crafting imaginative playsets, taking kids (and adults) on big adventures from the comfort of their homes. When it comes to the exploration of space, they've got a lot to offer. Not only has Playmobil created two mega Star Trek sets, releasing the Playmobil USS Enterprise long before LEGO released its own version and the Playmobil Klingon Bird of Prey back in 2023 (both of which we've reviewed and loved), but they've even collaborated with the real-life European Space Agency (ESA).

As Nadia Lüders, ESA 's partnership and brand licensing officer, said in a statement : “This partnership ensures that the curiosity and wonder of space continue to spark young imaginations — nurturing a new generation ready to explore, innovate and shape the Europe of tomorrow.”

Playmobil's dedication to weaving space exploration and learning into imaginative play is demonstrated in the sheer amount of space and sci-fi sets they have to offer, of which we'll jump into all 13 of them below. Ranging in price from the Playmobil Space Ranger for $15 to the Star Trek USS Enterprise for $354 , there are playsets for a range of ages, interests, and budgets.

Not a fan of Playmobil, or can't find the right set? We've also rated and ranked the best Lego Star Wars , Lego space , and Lego Marvel sets you can buy.

The best Star Trek Playmobil sets we recommend 2026

Playmobil USS Enterprise

(Image credit: Future) USS Enterprise

A sizeable Playmobil model of the original Enterprise, a treat for TOS fans.

Age rating: 10+ | Pieces: 150 | Figures: 6 | Dimensions: 39.4 x 18.9 x 13.4 in (100 x 48 x 34 cm) | Weight: 4.72 kg (10.4 lbs)

Gorgeous replica

Authentic lights and sounds

Easy to build

Expensive

Lots of stickers

Playmobil launched the Star Trek USS Enterprise years ahead of LEGO’s November 2025 release date, and it made us ask the question: Playmobil versus Lego, which is the best USS Enterprise set? For starters, the Playmobil set comes in cheaper. And while it’s got 150 pieces in comparison to Lego’s 3,600, it’s still a lot bigger, measuring over 3 feet (1 meter) in length.

When our expert testers gave the Playmobil Star Trek USS Enterprise a full review, it earned a whopping 4 ½ stars, delighting with its authentic light and sounds, and an ease of build that results in a gorgeous replica. Yes, it’s expensive and it has a lot of stickers, but if you’re a fan of both Star Trek and Playmobil, it’s an excellent model you can keep in your home forever. Recommended for ages 10 years and up.

Playmobil Klingon Bird of Prey

(Image credit: Brett Tingley) Klingon Bird of Prey

This set is considered a collectable but it's worth tracking down

Age rating: 10+ | Pieces: 94 | Figures: 6 | Dimensions: 19.5 x 23 x 7.25 in (49.5 x 58 x 18 cm) | Weight: 4.4 lbs (2 kg)

Impressively detailed

Great lights and sounds

Figurines are loads of fun

Some stickers are tiny

Playmobil followed up its Star Trek USS Enterprise with another impressive model, the Klingon Bird of Prey. Now considered a collectible, it’s a little harder to get your hands on, though we found it at an online toy store for $350.

If you’re wondering whether it’s worth the investment, in our expert Playmobil Klingon Bird of Prey review, we called this set “among the most impressive toys and models Space.com has had the pleasure of reviewing.” Impressive detail, great lights and sounds, and figurines that are a lot of fun are just some of the reasons we gave it 4.5/5 stars. And after the build is done, it looks fantastic on its included display.

It’s on the larger side, though (19.5 x 23 x 7.25 inches / 50 x 58 x 18 cm), so make sure you have room to display it before you buy. Recommended for ages 10 years and up.

Playmobil Star Trek figures

(Image credit: Playmobil) Playmobil Star Trek figures

This set is handy if you just want your own Playmobil away team.

Age rating: 10+ | Pieces: 10 | Figures: 4 | Dimensions: 9.76 x 5.59 x 1.81 in (24.79 x 14.20 x 4.60 cm) | Weight: 0.26 lbs (120 g)

To accompany your Star Trek investments, or just to have as part of a wider Playmobil space collection, you can also secure the four Playmobil Star Trek figurines. James T. Kirk, Mr. Spock, Dr. Leonard McCoy and Nyota Uhura all come in this pack alongside individual accessories.

Kirk comes with his phaser, Spock a tricorder disguised as a bag, McCoy with a so-called hypospray and Uhura with a skirt to change outfits. For any Trekkies, it's an affordable addition for any ultimate fan's collection. This one's recommended for ages 10 and up.

The best space ESA-collaborated Playmobil sets we recommend 2026

Playmobil ESA Starter Pack Space Mission

(Image credit: Playmobil) ESA Space Mission

Roam the lunar surface with this Playmobil rover

Age rating: 4+ | Pieces: 57 | Figures: 1 | Dimensions: 9.76 x 7.36 x 2.84 in (24.79 x 18.69 x 7.21 cm) | Weight: 0.48 lbs (216 g)

Playmobil and ESA have built a partnership, and an accompanying six different play sets, to inspire a love of intergalactic exploration. And the Starter Pack Space Mission is a great introduction to building out a Playmobil collection dedicated to all things space, especially as the sets can be mixed, matched and expanded.

In the pack, you get an astronaut figure, lunar rover with two lights, antenna, solar panel, satellite dish, rock samples and other accessories. Recommended for ages 4 years old and up, it's a gift for any space lover, whether they're a kid or adult.

There's also a nod to the ESA with the organization's logo emblazoned on both the rover and astronaut's spacesuit. As the production description states: "The astronaut discovered unusual soil samples during a tour with the lunar vehicle. The samples now have to be analyzed very quickly in the mobile station and the results transmitted via satellite. What will the results be?"

Playmobil ESA Astronaut with Robot

(Image credit: Playmobil) ESA Astronaut with Robot

A small, pocket-friendly Mars set with plenty of play value

Age rating: 4+ | Pieces: 42 | Figures: 1 | Dimensions: 3.66 x 5.59 x 1.77 in (9.30 x 14.20 x 4.50 cm) | Weight: 0.20 lbs (90 g)

A smaller set that works alongside the others in the Playmobil/ESA range, the Astronaut with Robot is a two-figure build consisting of 42 pieces. As the pack explains: “Together with his reliable companion robot and a nimble Mars crawler, the astronaut collects fascinating soil samples on the Red Planet.”

And you don’t only get a robot and astronaut (able to sit and stand) with the set, but a backpack, ground scanner analysis station, rock samples, base plate, gripper arm and more, too. Suitable for young explorers from age 4 years and up, it's an excellent addition to the larger Mars mission, working alongside the rest of the themed Playmobil sets.

Playmobil ESA Mars Exploration Rover

(Image credit: Playmobil) ESA Mars Exploration Rover

Playmobil's own version of the Mars Pathfinder, with astronaut friend

Age rating: 4+ | Pieces: 76 | Figures: 1 | Dimensions: 7.36 x 5.59 x 2.84 in (18.69 x 14.20 x 7.21 cm) | Weight: 0.64 lbs (290 g)

With the Playmobil ESA Mars Rover, you can launch your own mission to Mars in this 76-piece set. It comes with drill, cameras and high-tech sensors, as well as rock samples and other accessories to build your great space exploration adventure. And it's also focused on the types of powerful scientific instruments you'd find on the actual Mars Rover, as well as reenacting the way you'd store and analyze the samples.

As with any of these sets, imagination is key, but that's helped along with the inclusion of everything you need to bring authentic space exploration to life. The Playmobil ESA set is perfect for fans and includes rotating drills, movable cameras and a sturdy six-wheel drive to make discovery possible.

Playmobil ESA Space Glider

(Image credit: Playmobil) ESA Space Glider

A cool little space vehicle that offers a lot of fun for its pricetag
